newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian clashes force Shell to cut oil output.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian clashes force Shell to cut oil output.

text.p: Oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Friday that ethnic clashes had forced it to close some Forcados oil output and it had declared force majeure on some cargoes due for lifting from April 29th.
"Some 20 percent of Forcados blend crude has had to be shut in," a Shell spokesman told Reuters in Lagos. "We believe it will affect liftings due from April 29th," he added.
Traders said the reduction was equivalent to about 90,000 barrels per day of production.
The spokesman said the number of Shell staff in the troubled area had also been reduced.

Renewed clashes in the oil-producing swamps between militant youths of Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes over the relocation of a local council headquarters have claimed many lives and forced Shell to close its Warri flow station last weekend.
Five people, including a 75-year-old man who was beheaded, became the latest victims of the clashes in the oil-producing midwestern when it spread to the town of Koko from Warri.
Local newspapers said grenade-throwing youths on Wednesday night invaded Koko town near Warri which had been the scene of clashes until troops deployed there on Tuesday.
They said many houses were set ablaze and the hospital in the town was damaged. A gas pumping station belonging to the Nigerian Gas Company was sacked, forcing the workers to flee.
Defence headquarters spokesman Colonel Godwin Ugbo said he could not confirm the report.
"Peace has returned to Warri and the officer on ground knows what to do if the crisis spreads to a neighbouring town," he told Reuters in Lagos.

Warri, 300 km (190 miles) east of Lagos, has been the centre of communal fighting for the last month between militant youths over the transfer of the local council headquarters from an Ijaw town to a town of the rival Itsekiri tribe.

At the height of the crisis in March, armed Ijaw tribesmen occupied six oil flow stations of the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, shutting off 100,000 barrels per day of its crude oil production.
Some 127 of Shell's Nigerian staff held by the tribesmen were released after negotiations and oil production resumed.
At the root of the crisis is a long-standing rivalry among three tribes -- the Ijaws, the Itsekiris and the Urhobos.
